title: The Early Universe
description: Modern cosmology from first principles: the expanding universe, its dynamics and geometry, the hot Big Bang, the cosmic microwave background, the cosmological constant and dark energy, and inflation. It assumes single- and multivariable calculus (18.01, 18.02) and special relativity (8.033); the general relativity it needs is introduced as the course goes.

themes.title: The expanding universe
themes.blurb: Hubble's law, the scale factor, comoving coordinates and cosmological redshift: what it means for space itself to expand.

themes.title: Dynamics of expansion
themes.blurb: How gravity and the matter content decide the fate of the universe: the Friedmann equation, critical density and the age of the universe.

themes.title: Geometry of space and spacetime
themes.blurb: Closed, open and flat universes, the spacetime metric and the paths light and matter follow through curved space.

themes.title: The Big Bang and the cosmic microwave background
themes.blurb: Black-body radiation, the thermal history of the early universe and the afterglow released when atoms first formed.

themes.title: Dark energy
themes.blurb: The cosmological constant, vacuum energy and the Type Ia supernova evidence that the expansion is accelerating.

themes.title: Inflation
themes.blurb: The flatness, horizon and monopole problems of the conventional Big Bang, and the rapid early expansion that solves them.

themes.title: Dark matter
themes.blurb: Rotation curves, galaxy clusters, gravitational lensing and the CMB all point to matter we cannot see. Extra pages beyond MIT's lecture list; sources assigned per page.

themes.title: Structure formation
themes.blurb: How tiny density ripples grew by gravity into galaxies and the cosmic web. Extra pages beyond MIT's lecture list; sources assigned per page.

notes: Lecture titles are from the 8.286 Fall 2013 video lectures page. Dark matter and structure formation get their own pages beyond MIT's lecture list; each such page names its own MIT source.
